why: Both migrations are mechanically the same wrap-plus-policy and both correctly diagnose the two real blockers (seed=0, retired model ids), but A moved materially more traffic — aider's coding loops, the pipeline's biggest token consumer, plus prompt_cache_key in the migration itself — and is the only one with live Router evidence rather than simulator-only claims. A's system-level ladder is also deeper and better ranked for THIS app: per-stage feature labels as the enabling change, then a cheap model for the ~500-call novelty stage and cross-vendor fallbacks for an unattended GPU batch job that today loses hours of work to one 503, whereas B's three improvements stop at caching, ensemble fan-out and a cheaper reviewer and propose nothing for resilience or spend attribution.
A_best: It read past the static scan to find why nothing actually routed (seed, a two-year-old model list, and a pre-existing anthropic 1.13 TypeError that means the default Claude model produces zero traffic at all), fixed each in the right layer, verified live against real Router, and ranked its unbuilt work so the stage-label change unlocks per-stage model/cache/timeout policy as one-liners.
B_best: Sharper behaviour-preservation judgment: it names the specific loss others gloss over — the repo's published reviewer-agreement numbers are pinned to the May-2024 gpt-4o snapshot, and unpinning it lets OpenAI move the app — gives each trade-off a clean single-commit undo, and argues a correct negative on Flex (no routable model here has a Flex tier) instead of proposing it reflexively.
A_worst: Its biggest claimed win, routing aider through install_litellm, rests on one simulator request and covers only LiteLLM's OpenAI provider; it was never exercised live, and the Anthropic/DeepSeek/OpenRouter coder paths — the common configurations — silently stay off Router, so a single run can be half-routed. Its drop_params/model_map also sit in policy defaults rather than scoped to llm.py.
B_worst: It left the largest token consumer in the app (aider) entirely unmoved on a ROUTER.md caveat it did not test, had zero live verification of any routing claim, and proposed nothing about resilience or spend attribution for an unattended hours-long pipeline whose only error handling is an unbounded retry that discards an idea's GPU work on any 5xx.
